beats.headline: Another magic book
beats.text: Donut's final box, a platinum one, contains another magic book: a fifteen-mana spell called Wall of Fire. That's an escape spell, Mordecai says, a wall about ten metres wide and two metres high that lasts fifteen seconds at level one. It is common, and it grows powerful, but it is fire, and fire spreads: cast on something flammable, it stays on fire when the magic goes away. He has seen it a hundred times: fire gets out of control very easily. It's not Fireball, Donut grumbles. She glows as she reads the book.

beats.headline: Burning gerbils
beats.text: After ten solid minutes of fighting, the gerbils keep coming, and Donut casts Wall of Fire just as the next wave shoots at the defensive line. That is a mistake. The little bastards launch themselves through the air, and passing through the magical fire they ignite, turning into miniature, gnashing fireballs. The fire kills them, but not before they attach to the chests of the camel defenders and set them alight. By now they have been pushed all the way back to the entrance of Weird Shit Alley.

beats.headline: Inside Ghazi's room
beats.text: Katia cries Shell, and Carl flies back from the door and slams against the stairs. He hits Protective Shell just as Donut's Wall of Fire bursts up inside the room, and the door explodes. The fire catches the piles of books and tables at once. Ghazi runs into view, shouting, straight through the wall of the shell, trapped on their side of the flames. His dot is still white.

beats.headline: Bigger than ever
beats.text: There are too many mobs, Anton cries, his crossbow making little monkey noises with every shot, while Sister Ines lobs her white balls one after another. Donut casts Wall of Fire, which crackles bigger than ever thanks to her new nipple ring, and a pair of clockwork Mongos appear and tear through the mobs. Carl tosses two infused smoke curtains, and a holy gooper clears the way to the saferoom.

beats.headline: A mile of flame
beats.text: Skulls are flooding the streets ahead of the truck, leaving a narrower and narrower path to the finish line. Donut leans forward and casts her level 15 Wall of Fire, powered up to level 16. A line of flames appears on the passenger's side, running parallel with the truck about thirty feet away, and races ahead far into the distance. The flames go straight up, easily a hundred feet into the air. The line has to be a mile long.
